newsitem.title: USA: Judge throws out settlement against Liggett Group.
newsitem.headline: Judge throws out settlement against Liggett Group.

text.p: A federal judge threw out a preliminary class-action settlement against tobacco company Liggett Group Inc, a unit of Brooke Group Ltd, court officials said Friday.
The settlement would have affected claims by millions of people who have smoking-related illnesses.

A clerk in U.S. District Judge Charles Haden's office told Reuters that Haden this week withdrew his decision to expand a lawsuit by Putnam County resident Earl Walker Jr., who is suing Liggett Group, based in Durham, North Carolina.
Walker smoked Liggett-brand cigarettes for many years and has lung cancer. Liggett Group manufactures Chesterfield, Lark, and L&M cigarettes.
Haden said in his ruling that a class-action case would have exposed Liggett Group to an excessive number of claims.
Haden had granted preliminary approval to the class-action settlement last May.
The settlement would have prevented smokers, victims of secondhand smoke, states that pay Medicaid bills for smoking diseases and others nationwide from suing Liggett Group for 25 years.
The company, in turn, would have paid 25 percent of its net pre-tax profits for the next 25 years to people suffering from smoking-related illnesses.
Attorneys for Walker and Liggett Group were unavailable for comment.
Separately, Haden scheduled a hearing on August 26 for Walker's lawsuit against the tobacco company.
